content: 1. When prescribing medications that have weight gain as a potential side effect, it is essential to use the lowest effective dose, particularly in patients with coexisting medical conditions. 2. In individuals diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, prioritize the use of glucose-lowering medications that are either weight-neutral or promote weight loss. 3. Pharmacological treatment for obesity is recommended for patients with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher, or a BMI of 27 or higher if they have weight-related complications, especially when lifestyle interventions alone have not been successful. 4. For obesity pharmacotherapy, GLP-1 receptor agonists and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists are preferred due to their proven efficacy in achieving significant weight loss. 5. To optimize treatment outcomes, combine weight management medications with structured lifestyle modifications and behavioral interventions.
